newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat market quiet, awaits Algeria, Iraq.
newsitem.headline: French wheat market quiet, awaits Algeria, Iraq.

text.p: The French wheat market was subdued on Monday, with operators awaiting the outcome of import tenders launched by Algeria and Iraq, dealers said.
Wheat prices retreated slightly from levels reached on Friday after the U.S. Agriculture Department released bullish grain and oilseeds crop and stocks data.
Prompt wheat into Rouen was bid at 855 francs per tonne, down five on Friday.
Rouen wheat for February-March was offered at 852.50 francs per tonne, a level paid on Friday after the USDA report hit the market.
"The rally quickly ran out of steam," one dealer said.
U.S. grain and oilseeds futures markets soared on Friday after the USDA cut its final estimates of 1996 crops and grain stocks and reported a sharp fall in wheat plantings.
Algeria is in the market to import 75,000 tonnes of optional soft wheat for February and March, traders said earlier.
Iraq is seeking 100,000 tonnes of French wheat for March and April.
The deadline for offers is January 13 for the Algerian tender and January 14 for the Iraqi tender.
